query: The Far Bell {The bell for your lecture is ringing in the other tower, and you are on the wrong side of the bridge with all your books.|The bell again, and you on the wrong end of the bridge again. You're starting to suspect the bridge.|You can hear the bell before you see the bridge. Seven strokes; it's on the third.} Run for it {You slide into your seat on the last stroke with your books in a heap. The lecturer looks at the clock, then at you, then lets it go.|You make it, red-faced and triumphant. Your neighbour pushes a quill at you without a word.|You know the run now: left foot on the second plank, duck the lamp. In with a stroke to spare.} {You drop your books halfway across the bridge and arrive five minutes late with half of them.|You arrive as the door closes, and spend the hour listening through it. It's not the same.|You trip on the top step and the whole lecture turns to watch you pick up your inkwell.} Arrive late, quietly {You walk, and slip in at the back ten minutes late. You miss the one thing that'll be on the exam.|You arrive late and sit on the end of the back row, where the notes from the front arrive late too.|Late, and calm, and behind for the rest of the hour. Someone lends you their notes afterwards, in a hand you can't read.} Borrow a hare's legs {You cross the bridge in four strides with the wind whistling, and sit down before the bell has finished. Your books arrive a moment later, in your arms.|Haste, and the bridge goes by in a blur of light. You're in your seat, notes open, looking as if you've been there an hour.|{spell_level(haste) >= 2: You're early. You've time to sharpen a quill and help a first-year find the room.|You arrive breathless but on the stroke. The lecturer says "Prompt," which from them is warm.}}
